land.text: the lordship of Bourbon (Bourbonnais), whose Sires de Bourbon ran from 913 to 1327 and which 'In 1327, King Charles (le Bel) elevated ... to the status of a duchy'

predecessors.note: The lordship was a vassal of the French king (House page: 'vassals of the French king from at least the early 13th century'); Cliopatria has no earlier Bourbon row.

land.text: the Bourbon lands of Henry III of Navarre on his accession as Henry IV on 2 August 1589; the Bourbon duchy itself had been sequestered in 1523 and merged into the royal domain in 1531

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the row to 1594 (the coronation at Chartres, 27 February 1594); the Henry IV page's infobox merges the Vendome titles into the crown on 2 August 1589.

capitals.name: Moulins
capitals.note: 'Its capital and seat is Moulins' (Bourbonnais page, no dates); Jeanne d'Albret and Antoine were married at Moulins in 1548. Coordinates are the modern town, not read from a page. The state holds no land and has no seat in 1524-1526.

capitals.name: Vendôme
capitals.note: No page opened names a seat for the Bourbon-Vendome line after the 1523 sequestration; the duchy of Vendome (raised from a county in 1514) stands in, from 1527 when the line becomes the senior one. Charles of Vendome governed Picardy from La Fere (Charles, Duke of Vendome page); Antoine was born at La Fere. Coordinates are the modern town, not read from a page.

capitals.name: Pau
capitals.note: 'Their joint coronation followed at Pau on 18 August 1555' (Jeanne d'Albret page); Pau became the Bearnese capital in 1464 (Bearn page). Coordinates are the modern town, not read from a page.

rulers.name: John I
rulers.title: Duke of Bourbon; Duke of Auvergne from 1416

rulers.name: Suzanne
rulers.title: Duchess of Bourbon
rulers.note: The table gives Charles III as duke from 1505, the year of his marriage; the strip lists her for her own years.

rulers.name: Charles III
rulers.title: Duke of Bourbon (duke from 1505 by marriage; table end 1523)
rulers.note: Sequestered in August 1523, he fled, held no land in France and died on 6 May 1527 at Rome; his title was discontinued after his death and the senior line was extinct in the male line in 1527 (House page).

rulers.name: Charles of Bourbon, Duke of Vendome
rulers.title: head of the Bourbon-Vendome branch, the senior branch from 1527
rulers.note: Born 2 June 1489, died at Amiens on 25 March 1537; the county of Vendome was raised to a duchy in 1514 (House page) or March 1515 (his page).

rulers.name: Antoine de Bourbon
rulers.title: Duke of Vendome from 25 March 1537
rulers.note: Born 22 April 1518 at La Fere; married Jeanne d'Albret at Moulins on 20 October 1548.

rulers.name: Jeanne III of Navarre and Antoine de Bourbon
rulers.title: joint rulers of Navarre from 25 May 1555
rulers.note: 'On 25 May 1555, Jeanne and her husband, Antoine, became joint rulers' (Jeanne d'Albret page); Antoine reigned as King of Navarre jure uxoris 25 May 1555 - 17 November 1562 (Antoine of Navarre page).

rulers.name: Henry III of Navarre (Henry IV of France)
rulers.title: King of Navarre; King of France from 2 August 1589

correction.text: the duchy of Bourbon (Bourbonnais) raised in 1327 together with La Marche, which passed to the house in 1327 (or 1322); same lands as Cliopatria's 1333 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1333. 'In 1327, King Charles (le Bel) elevated the Bourbonnais to the status of a duchy'; the County of La Marche page has 'in 1327, La Marche passed into the hands of the House of Bourbon' (its list says 1322 for the exchange with Clermont).

1333-1351 in Cliopatria. The County of La Marche list gives 'Louis I of Bourbon (1322-1341)', then 'James I of Bourbon (1341-1362)'; the House of Bourbon page: 'The remaining line of Bourbons henceforth descended from James I, Count of La Marche, the younger son of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon'; the Duke of Bourbon table gives Peter I as duke 1341-1356. Rule of this dossier: land counts while the Duke of Bourbon holds it in person (the ducal domain). La Marche leaves that domain in 1341, so the shape runs ten years short of Cliopatria's 1351. No page opened gives an area to compare (the Bourbonnais page: 'the modern Allier departement, plus part of Cher').

correction.text: unchanged shape, 18,782 km2 (the Bourbonnais plus La Marche), but holding 1333-1341 only: La Marche passes to James I of Bourbon, 'the younger son of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon', in 1341
the Bourbonnais alone (8,482 km2, Allier 88%), as Cliopatria's 1363 shape; La Marche belongs to James I's cadet line

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's 1333 shape still carries La Marche in 1342-1351 and its 1352 shape to 1362, 21 years after the page's list passes the county from Louis I (1322-1341) to James I of Bourbon (1341-1362). The shape for these years is the Bourbonnais of Cliopatria's 1363 shape.

1352-1362 in Cliopatria, 18,828 km2 with La Marche. The county went to James I in 1341 and stayed in his line (Peter II of Bourbon-La Marche 1362, John I 1362-1393 on the same list), not to the dukes Peter I (1341-1356) and Louis II (1356-1410); see the 1333 and 1342 keyframes.

correction.text: the Bourbonnais alone, as Cliopatria's 1363 shape, 8,482 km2, holding 1352-1362 (Cliopatria's 1352 shape, 18,828 km2, still carries La Marche)

keyframe_review.note: 1363-1374, 8,482 km2: the Bourbonnais alone (Allier 88%), the shape this dossier uses for 1342-1374. The list's 1362 entries ('Peter II of Bourbon-La Marche (1362)', 'John I of Bourbon-La Marche (1362-1393)') are the cadet line's own succession from James I (1341-1362); nothing leaves the ducal domain in 1362, so Cliopatria's 1363 step is 22 years behind the 1341 loss.

correction.text: unchanged shape, the Bourbonnais plus Forez (the Loire department and western Rhone cells), but holding from 1372, when Louis II became Count of Forez

keyframe_review.note: 1375-1384, 13,712 km2: Forez added. The Louis II page: married Anne of Auvergne, daughter of Beraud II and the Countess of Forez, on 19 August 1371 and was 'Count of Forez, with Anna' 1372-1410. The shape starts three years late; the 1363 shape therefore holds to 1371 (from 1342, see the 1342 keyframe).

1385-1394, 14,543 km2: the 1375 lands with a slightly larger Forez polygon (Loire 71% against 67%); an edge shift, no page opened dates a change in 1385. Beaujolais and Dombes, which the 1375-1407 shapes do not carry (their Rhone cells lie at 45.74-46.02 N, the southern edge of the Beaujolais and the Monts du Lyonnais, and no cell is in the Ain), come in 1400 and 1402 (Dombes page; see the 1400 keyframe).

1395-1401 in Cliopatria. 'In 1400, Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, acquired the northern part of the Dombes, together with the lordship of Beaujeu' (Dombes page). The shape has 6 Rhone cells (4.46-4.93 E, 45.74-46.02 N, the southern edge of the Beaujolais and the Monts du Lyonnais) and no Ain cell, so it carries neither the lordship of Beaujeu in full nor the Dombes.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 14,496 km2, but holding 1395-1399 only: the lordship of Beaujeu and the northern Dombes come in 1400
the 1395 shape plus the lordship of Beaujeu (Beaujolais, northern Rhone) and the northern part of the Dombes (Ain)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1400, Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, acquired the northern part of the Dombes, together with the lordship of Beaujeu'. No page gives their extent: Beaujolais is the Rhone cells within 25 km of about 4.6 E, 46.1 N and the northern Dombes the Ain cells within 22 km of 5.0 E, 46.2 N inside a 25 km radius of 4.95 E, 46.0 N; both are stand-ins whose centres are not read from a page.

1402-1406 in Cliopatria. The Dombes page: the duke 'two years later bought the southern part from the sires de Thoire', forming a sovereign principality with Trevoux as capital; Cliopatria's 1402 shape has no Ain cell and shifts only an edge cell.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 14,427 km2, plus Beaujolais and the whole of the Dombes, holding 1402-1406
unchanged shape, 14,334 km2, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, but holding 1407-1415 only: Auvergne comes in 1416

keyframe_review.note: 1407-1421 in Cliopatria; 'In 1416, with the death of John of Valois, the Dukes of Bourbon were simultaneously Dukes of Auvergne' (the Duke of Bourbon page), six years before the 1422 shape adds Auvergne. Beaujolais and the Dombes are added from the 1400 and 1402 acquisitions (Dombes page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 33,331 km2 (the Bourbon lands plus Auvergne: Puy-de-Dome, Cantal, Haute-Loire), plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, but holding from 1416

keyframe_review.note: 1422-1452 in Cliopatria. The page dates the Bourbon dukes' Auvergne to 1416; the Duke of Berry page gives 'Duke of Auvergne 1360-1416', succeeded by his daughter Marie of Berry, who later married John I, Duke of Bourbon. Cliopatria's County of Auvergne row (1206-1501) overlaps this land. Beaujolais and the Dombes are added (Dombes page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 33,331 km2 without La Marche, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, holding 1453-1481 (La Marche is not the duke's until 1488)

keyframe_review.note: 1453-1481 in Cliopatria, no change inside it. 'The family of Armagnac held it from 1435 to 1477, when it reverted to the Bourbons' and 'In 1477, Jacques was convicted of treason and his territories were confiscated by Louis XI' (La Marche page), but the list gives the county to Peter II of Bourbon (1477-1503), who was not duke until 1488 (Duke of Bourbon table), so under this dossier's ducal-domain rule it joins in 1488. Beaujolais and the Dombes are added (Dombes page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 33,309 km2 without La Marche, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, holding 1482-1487

keyframe_review.note: 1482-1491 in Cliopatria, without La Marche. Peter II held La Marche from 1477 but became Duke of Bourbon only in 1488 (Duke of Bourbon table: Charles II 1488, Peter II 1488-1503), so the shape holds to 1487 and the 1492 shape starts in 1488.

1492-1496 in Cliopatria, 43,380 km2: Bourbon lands, Auvergne and La Marche (Creuse 100%, Haute-Vienne 50%). Peter II becomes duke in 1488 and holds La Marche 1477-1503 (La Marche list), so the ducal domain has it from 1488, four years before the shape starts.

correction.text: unchanged shape, 43,380 km2 (the Bourbon lands, Auvergne and La Marche), plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, but holding from 1488

keyframe_review.note: 1497-1518, 43,426 km2, the same lands. The marriage of 10 May 1505 united the lines: 'Bourbon would in his life hold the comte de Montpensier, the duches de Bourbon, Auvergne and Chatellerault; the comtes de Forez, La Marche, Beaujolais, and Clermont-en-Beauvaisis', with the principality of Dombes (Charles III page); the shape shows no change in 1505. Beaujolais and the Dombes are added (Dombes page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 43,426 km2, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes

keyframe_review.note: 1519-1520, 43,449 km2, the same lands; Suzanne drew up her will in favour of her husband on 15 December 1519. Beaujolais and the Dombes are added (Dombes page).

correction.text: unchanged shape, 43,449 km2, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes
unchanged shape, 43,564 km2, plus Beaujolais and the Dombes, but holding 1521-1522 only: 'In August 1523, all the disputed lands were sequestered from Bourbon'

keyframe_review.note: 1521-1555 in Cliopatria. Suzanne died in 1521; Francis I and his mother Louise disputed her will; the lands were sequestered in August 1523 and Charles III held nothing in France until his death on 6 May 1527 at Rome, so the state has no land in 1523-1526 (no keyframe; the Vendome stand-in starts in 1527). La Marche 'was seized by Francis I' in 1527 (La Marche page) and 'In 1531, the duchy merged into the royal domain' (Duke of Bourbon page). The shape is wrong for 1523-1555.

correction.text: the Bourbon-Vendome branch's duchy of Vendome (a county raised to a duchy in 1514), the senior branch from 1527; a stand-in radius, since no page opened describes its extent

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the years Cliopatria still draws the sequestered Bourbon domain. House page: 'In 1514, Charles, Count of Vendome had his title raised to Duke of Vendome' (the Charles, Duke of Vendome page says March 1515); the senior line 'became extinct in the male line in 1527' and the Bourbon-Vendome branch became 'the genealogically senior branch'. Charles of Vendome (d. 25 March 1537) governed Picardy 'from the chateau de La Fere'; his son Antoine was Duke of Vendome from 25 March 1537 (Antoine of Navarre page) and married Jeanne d'Albret at Moulins on 20 October 1548. The state holds nothing in 1523-1526: the sequestered domain went to the crown and Charles III, in exile, died on 6 May 1527.

correction.text: the Navarre-Albret domain of Jeanne III and Antoine (Navarre and Lower Navarre, Bearn, Foix, Bigorre, Armagnac, Albret, Perigord, Limoges and Soule) plus Vendome: Cliopatria's 74,189 km2 shape with the sequestered Bourbon domain (its 1521 shape) removed; held from May 1555, when Jeanne and Antoine succeed, not Cliopatria's 1556

keyframe_review.note: 1556-1563 in Cliopatria (74,189 km2); the accession is 25 May 1555, so the shape is held from 1555. The shape adds the south-west (Pyrenees-Atlantiques 61%, Dordogne 76%, Correze, Lot-et-Garonne, Hautes-Pyrenees, Ariege) to the Bourbon lands that had been sequestered in 1523 and merged into the crown in 1531, so it is the 1521 shape plus Jeanne's lands. 'On 25 May 1555, Jeanne and her husband, Antoine, became joint rulers after her father's death'; lands listed: Navarre, Bearn, Foix, Bigorre, Armagnac, Albret, Perigord, Limoges, Vendome, Lower Navarre and Soule.

correction.text: as for 1556: the Navarre-Albret domain without the sequestered Bourbon lands, plus Vendome

keyframe_review.note: 1564-1587, 74,304 km2, the same polygon as 1556. Jeanne III publicly embraced Calvinism on Christmas Day 1560 and died on 9 June 1572; her son became King Henry III of Navarre.

correction.text: as for 1556, but holding to 2 August 1589 only

keyframe_review.note: 1588-1594 in Cliopatria. Henry accedes as Henry IV on 2 August 1589; the infobox lists the Vendome, Beaumont, Marle, La Fere and Soissons titles ending that day, 'Merged into the crown', and the Albret, Foix and Armagnac titles ending the same day without that label. He was crowned at Chartres on 27 February 1594. The page does not say whether Bearn or Navarre were merged.

region.text: the Bourbonnais, raised to a duchy

ledger.note: 1327: King Charles (le Bel) raises the Bourbonnais to a duchy for Louis I. 'In 1327, King Charles (le Bel) elevated the Bourbonnais to the status of a duchy'; the House page: 'Their son Louis was made Duke of Bourbon in 1327'. The sires of Bourbon ran from 913; the long-lasting House began with Beatrice's marriage to Robert de France in 1272. Capital Moulins.

region.text: the County of La Marche (Haute and Basse Marche)

ledger.note: 1327: La Marche comes to the Bourbons. 'Several years later in 1327, La Marche passed into the hands of the House of Bourbon' (the page's list dates the exchange with Louis of Bourbon for Clermont to 1322, on Charles's accession). The region is Cliopatria's 1492-minus-1482 cells. Rule of this dossier: land counts while the Duke of Bourbon holds it in person (the ducal domain); a count or cadet who is not duke holds it outside the domain.

region.text: La Marche, which passes to the Duke's younger son James

ledger.counterpart: County of La Marche (James I of Bourbon)
ledger.note: 1341: La Marche leaves the ducal domain for the cadet line. The page's list gives 'Louis I of Bourbon (1322-1341)', then 'James I of Bourbon (1341-1362)'; the House of Bourbon page calls James I 'the younger son of Louis I, Duke of Bourbon', and the Duke of Bourbon table makes Peter I duke 1341-1356. The county then passes within the cadet line (Peter II of Bourbon-La Marche 1362, John I 1362-1393, James II 1393-1438), so nothing changes hands in 1362; Cliopatria drops it from the Bourbon shape only in 1363. The County of La Marche needs its own dossier.

region.text: Forez (the Loire department with the western Rhone cells)

ledger.note: 1372: Louis II becomes Count of Forez by marriage. He married Anne of Auvergne, daughter of Beraud II, Dauphin of Auvergne, and the Countess of Forez, on 19 August 1371; the succession table lists him as 'Count of Forez, with Anna' 1372-1410. The page says Louis was also Count of Clermont-en-Beauvaisis 1371-1400.

1400: Louis II acquires the lordship of Beaujeu. 'In 1400, Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, acquired the northern part of the Dombes, together with the lordship of Beaujeu.' The region is the Rhone cells within 25 km of about 4.6 E, 46.1 N (centre not read from a page), a stand-in; the page does not name the seller, and the Beaujolais page opened earlier names only Beaujeu as historical capital. The French Beaujolais page would not load.

region.text: the northern part of the Dombes

ledger.counterpart: Northern Dombes (holders not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1400: Louis II acquires the northern Dombes with the lordship of Beaujeu ('acquired the northern part of the Dombes, together with the lordship of Beaujeu'). The split between northern and southern Dombes is a stand-in: the Ain cells north of about 46.05 N.

region.text: the southern part of the Dombes

ledger.note: 1402: Louis II buys the southern Dombes. The page: 'two years later bought the southern part from the sires de Thoire', forming a sovereign principality with Trevoux as capital; 1402 is the page's two years after 1400.

region.text: the duchy of Auvergne, John of Valois's

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Auvergne (John, Duke of Berry)
ledger.note: 1416: the Dukes of Bourbon become Dukes of Auvergne. 'In 1416, with the death of John of Valois, the Dukes of Bourbon were simultaneously Dukes of Auvergne.' John of Valois is John, Duke of Berry, 'Duke of Auvergne 1360-1416', who died on 15 June 1416 and was succeeded by his daughter Marie of Berry, who later married John I, Duke of Bourbon (Duke of Berry page); the Bourbon page gives the year. The Cliopatria shape that carries Auvergne starts in 1422. Cliopatria's County of Auvergne row has no shape between 1407 and 1439, so that dossier holds no matching loss.

region.text: the County of La Marche, held by Peter II of Bourbon since 1477

ledger.counterpart: County of La Marche (Peter II of Bourbon)
ledger.note: 1488: La Marche joins the ducal domain when Peter II becomes Duke of Bourbon (Duke of Bourbon table: 1488-1503). The page: 'The family of Armagnac held it from 1435 to 1477, when it reverted to the Bourbons'; 'In 1477, Jacques was convicted of treason and his territories were confiscated by Louis XI of France', and the list gives Peter II of Bourbon as holder 1477-1503. He held it first in his own right, as a younger son of Charles I, so under the ducal-domain rule used for the 1341 loss it counts from 1488. The region is Cliopatria's 1492-minus-1482 cells.

10 May 1505: Charles de Bourbon (Montpensier) marries Suzanne de Bourbon and the ducal lands pass to him (duke 1505-1523, Duke of Bourbon table). 'Bourbon would in his life hold the comte de Montpensier, the duches de Bourbon, Auvergne and Chatellerault; the comtes de Forez, La Marche, Beaujolais, and Clermont-en-Beauvaisis', with the principality of Dombes. The lands stay together; the line changes from the Bourbon-Beaujeu duke to the Montpensier branch.

region.text: all the Bourbon lands in dispute after Suzanne's death: the duchy of Bourbon, Auvergne, Forez, La Marche, Beaujolais, the Dombes and the rest

ledger.note: August 1523: Francis I sequesters the Bourbon lands. 'In August 1523, all the disputed lands were sequestered from Bourbon'; Charles III fled to the Emperor and died on 6 May 1527 at Rome. 'The principality [of Dombes] was confiscated by King Francis I of France in 1523' (Dombes page; returned to the Bourbon-Montpensier family in 1560 per the Charles III page, granted to Louis, duc de Montpensier in 1561 per the Dombes page). La Marche 'was seized by Francis I' in 1527 (La Marche page) and 'In 1531, the duchy merged into the royal domain' (Duke of Bourbon page). From August 1523 to May 1527 the state holds no land in France.

1527: the senior line ends and the Bourbon-Vendome branch becomes the senior one. 'The senior line of the House of Bourbon became extinct in the male line in 1527' (Charles III died 6 May 1527); the Bourbon-Vendome branch, whose count was made Duke of Vendome in 1514, became 'the genealogically senior branch of the House of Bourbon'. The state holds nothing in 1523-1526; from 1527 it is the Vendome branch's land.

region.text: the duchy of Vendome, raised from a county in 1514

ledger.note: 1527: the dossier passes to the Bourbon-Vendome branch and its duchy of Vendome. House page: 'In 1514, Charles, Count of Vendome had his title raised to Duke of Vendome' and, on the senior line's extinction in 1527, the Bourbon-Vendome branch became 'the genealogically senior branch'. The Charles, Duke of Vendome page dates the elevation to March 1515 and has him governing Picardy from La Fere; no page opened gives the extent of the duchy, so a 25 km radius around Vendome stands in.

region.text: Bearn proper (bordered by Soule and Lower Navarre to the west, Gascony to the north, Bigorre to the east and Aragon to the south), drawn as the Pyrenees-Atlantiques cells within 50 km of Pau, plus Bigorre (the Hautes-Pyrenees) and the Nebouzan and eastern lands of Cliopatria's polygon (eastern Hautes-Pyrenees and south-west Haute-Garonne)

ledger.note: 25 May 1555: Jeanne III and Antoine of Bourbon become joint rulers of the Albret domain, Bearn among it. 'On 25 May 1555, Jeanne and her husband, Antoine, became joint rulers after her father's death'; the lands listed include Bearn and Bigorre, and the Antoine of Navarre page lists him as King of Navarre, Count of Foix, Bigorre, Armagnac and Perigord, and Viscount of Bearn. Their joint coronation followed at Pau on 18 August 1555. The page does not say how Bearn's own sovereignty was treated. The region is the same spec as the county-of-bearn dissolve event.
1555: Foix comes with Jeanne's inheritance (Foix is in the page's list of her lands); Cliopatria's County of Foix row also ends in 1555.

region.text: Navarre north of the Pyrenees (Lower Navarre), Soule, Armagnac, Albret, Perigord and Limoges

ledger.counterpart: Kingdom of Navarre and the House of Albret (Henry II of Navarre)
ledger.note: 1555: the rest of the Albret inheritance. 'Navarre, Bearn, Foix, Bigorre, Armagnac, Albret, Perigord, Limoges (Limousin), and Vendome, along with Lower Navarre and Soule'; the House page: Antoine 'became King of Navarre, on the northern side of the Pyrenees, by marriage in 1555'. The region is Cliopatria's 1556 shape minus its 1521 shape and minus Bearn (Bearn proper, the Hautes-Pyrenees and the Nebouzan polygon) and Ariege; Lower Navarre and Soule, east of the Basque coast, stay in it because Bearn is now drawn without them. The county-of-armagnac row ends in 1496.

region.text: the Bourbon lands of Henry III of Navarre

ledger.note: 2 August 1589: Henry III of Navarre becomes Henry IV of France and his Bourbon titles merge into the crown. 'On 2 August 1589, a monk infiltrated Henry III's camp and assassinated him'; the infobox ends the Vendome, Beaumont, Marle, La Fere and Soissons titles that day, 'Merged into the crown', and the Albret, Foix and Armagnac titles too (unlabelled). He was crowned at Chartres on 27 February 1594; Navarre passed to Louis II only at his death in 1610.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War
wars.outcome: Louis II led royal armies in Poitou and Guyenne to recover lands lost after the Treaty of Brétigny (1360): he took Limoges with the Duke of Berry in 1371 and strongholds in Rouergue, Poitou and Touraine in 1374; the Truce of Leulinghem followed in 1389. No Bourbon border moved.
wars.note: The Louis II page does not name the war; the standard name is used. He was a hostage in England from 1360 to 1367.

wars.name: Charles III's campaigns for Charles V
wars.outcome: After the sequestration of August 1523 Charles III fled France, helped repel a French attempt on Milan, led an invasion of Provence that stalled before Marseille and fought at Pavia, where Francis I was captured; he died at the Sack of Rome on 6 May 1527. His lands stayed with the crown.
wars.note: The page does not name the war; the name is descriptive.

certainty.note: Feudal and apanage lands with no survey or treaty line in the pages opened; Cliopatria's polygons for the Bourbonnais and its additions are approximate (Allier only 88% covered). The 1555 Albret lands are named by province and are drawn from a Cliopatria polygon, not a frontier. The Vendome stand-in (1527-1554), the Beaujolais and Dombes regions and the 1555 Bearn polygon are radii and cell sets, not frontiers; 1523-1526 has no land.

sources.title: House of Bourbon
sources.note: 1272 origin, 1327 duchy, James I as the younger son of Louis I, 1514 Vendome, 1527 extinction of the senior line, Navarre 1555, Henry IV; thin on the dukes' lands.

sources.title: Bourbonnais
sources.note: 913 to 1327, the 1327 duchy, Moulins as seat; silent on La Marche, Forez, Beaujolais, Auvergne and 1523-1531.

sources.title: Duke of Bourbon
sources.note: Table of dukes 1327-1523 (Peter I 1341-1356, Peter II 1488-1503), Auvergne 1416, 1523 stripping, 1531 merger into the royal domain; silent on La Marche, Forez, Beaujolais and Dombes.

sources.title: County of La Marche
sources.note: La Marche 1322/1327 to the Bourbons, 'James I of Bourbon (1341-1362)' after Louis I (1322-1341), the cadet line to 1393-1438, the Armagnacs 1435/1438-1477, Peter II 1477-1503, 1527 seizure by Francis I; does not say how James I was related to Louis I (the House page does).

sources.title: Charles III, Duke of Bourbon
sources.note: 1505 marriage and the lands held (Montpensier, Bourbon, Auvergne, Chatellerault, Forez, La Marche, Beaujolais, Clermont-en-Beauvaisis, Dombes), 1523 sequestration, death 6 May 1527; Dombes 'returned to the Bourbon-Montpensier family in 1560'.

sources.title: Louis II, Duke of Bourbon
sources.note: Marriage 1371, Count of Forez 1372, campaigns; silent on Beaujolais and Dombes.

sources.title: Jeanne d'Albret

sources.note: 1400: northern Dombes with the lordship of Beaujeu; two years later the southern part from the sires de Thoire; confiscated by Francis I in 1523; 1561 grant to Louis, duc de Montpensier; 1762 to the crown. (The title 'Principality of Dombes' did not load.)

sources.title: Charles, Duke of Vendome
sources.note: Born 2 June 1489, died 25 March 1537; Vendome county raised to a duchy in March 1515; governor of Picardy from La Fere; father of Antoine.

sources.title: Antoine of Navarre
sources.note: Duke of Vendome 25 March 1537 - 17 November 1562; married Jeanne d'Albret 20 October 1548; King of Navarre jure uxoris from 25 May 1555; titles Count of Foix, Bigorre, Armagnac and Perigord, Viscount of Bearn.

sources.title: John, Duke of Berry
sources.note: Duke of Auvergne 1360-1416, died 15 June 1416, succeeded by his daughter Marie of Berry, who later married John I, Duke of Bourbon.

notes: Cliopatria's 'House of Bourbon' is a dynastic domain whose polygon follows the ducal Bourbon lands (Bourbonnais, La Marche, Forez, Auvergne) to 1555 and then the Albret-Navarre lands of the Vendome line; the Wikipedia title is the house, not a state. RULE of this dossier: land counts while the Duke of Bourbon holds it in person (the ducal domain). A cadet or a count who is not duke holds land outside it: La Marche goes to James I, Louis I's younger son, in 1341 and stays in his line and the Armagnacs' until 1477; Peter II holds it from 1477 but is duke only from 1488, so it counts from 1488. Corrections made: (1) the state starts in 1327, not 1333, with a new keyframe; (2) La Marche leaves the domain in 1341 (La Marche list and House page), not 1362, so Cliopatria's 1333 and 1352 shapes hold 1333-1341 and the 1363 shape (the Bourbonnais alone) holds 1342-1374; (3) Forez 1372, Auvergne 1416 and La Marche 1488 are page dates that Cliopatria's 1375, 1422 and 1492 steps lag; (4) Beaujolais (lordship of Beaujeu) and the northern Dombes come in 1400 and the southern Dombes in 1402 (Dombes page), which no Cliopatria shape carries (no Ain cell, no Rhone cell north of 46.02 N), so they are added to every shape from 1400 to 1522; (5) the Bourbon domain was sequestered in August 1523 and merged into the royal domain in 1531, so the 1521 shape holds 1521-1522 only and Cliopatria's 1521-1555 and 1556-1594 shapes wrongly keep it; (6) from August 1523 to May 1527 the state holds no land in France (Charles III in exile, died 6 May 1527): no keyframe and no capital for 1523-1526; the Vendome stand-in runs 1527-1554, from the year the House page gives for the Bourbon-Vendome branch becoming the senior one; (7) the post-1555 shapes are Cliopatria's 1556 shape minus its 1521 shape plus Vendome, held from May 1555; (8) the row ends on 2 August 1589 (Henry IV page), not 1594. The ruler strip is the Duke of Bourbon table to 1523, Charles III to his death in 1527, Charles of Vendome (to 25 March 1537) and Antoine (Duke of Vendome from that date), the joint reign of Jeanne III and Antoine from 25 May 1555 to Antoine's death on 17 November 1562, then Jeanne and Henry. Not dated by any page opened: the Cliopatria edge shifts of 1385, 1395 and 1402; the head and seat of the Bourbon-Vendome line before 1537 beyond the dates above; any restitution of Bourbon-Montpensier lands after 1560 beyond Dombes (1560 per Charles III page, 1561 per Dombes page). Pages that failed: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Dombes and https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaujolais_(province) (url_not_found; the Dombes article loads as /wiki/Dombes). Overlaps: the Cliopatria County of Auvergne row (1206-1501), the Kingdom of France row and County of Foix (ends 1555). States that need a dossier: County of La Marche, County of Forez, Duchy of Vendome, Principality of Dombes, the Albret domain / Kingdom of Navarre north of the Pyrenees (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Navarre row ends 1428), and the Duchy of Auvergne of John, Duke of Berry (1360-1416). The place 'Vendome' is not in the gazetteer; the Beaujolais and Dombes regions are radii around about 4.6 E, 46.1 N and 4.95 E, 46.0 N (centres not read from pages) intersected with Rhone and Ain. The pages give no area figure; the Bourbonnais page says the old province is 'the modern Allier departement, plus part of Cher'. Capital coordinates are modern town centres, not read from pages.
